verdict.text: The change does what the plan asks.
Apply triage now takes the response file path from env RESPONSE_FILE and quotes "$RESPONSE_FILE" in its run line.
No run: in either Hermes workflow expands a step output, and the new tests fail if one does.
Read the staged diff: one workflow step and two tests in tests/scripts/test_workflows.py.
Grepped both Hermes workflows for `steps.`: the only uses left are env values (ISSUE_NUM twice, RESPONSE_FILE), none in a run: line.
Row r1: the parametrized test joins every run: of every job in both workflows through `_runs` and asserts `${{ steps.` is absent.
The second test asserts RESPONSE_FILE's env value and the quoted `"$RESPONSE_FILE"` in run.
I parsed the pre-change workflow from HEAD and found a run: holding `${{ steps.`, so the first test would have failed there; the row's fails_when holds.
scripts/hermes_triage.py already takes the path as its first argument, so the call contract is unchanged.
No doc or docstring describes the old line.
Re-ran `loopctl gate stamp` from the worktree: lint, format, tests, integration and eval-row r1 all pass; "stamp green: a43f107c88b8643771a53f645d13c677a364b48e5018294cda8c3728e959bf87".
